## Perspective Audit Summary **Component/artifact reviewed:** `SubscribePage` / `SubscribeModal` (React JSX + CSS) **Perspectives escalated for deep review:** Keyboard & Motor Access (HIGH), Screen Reader & Semantic Structure (HIGH), Cognitive & Neurodivergent (MEDIUM) **Perspectives at LOW (not reviewed):** Magnification & Reflow, Environmental Contrast, Vestibular & Motion Sensitivity, Auditory Access ### Detailed Findings by Escalated Perspective #### Keyboard & Motor Access ``` **Finding:** Focus escapes the modal to background navigation links when tabbing forward. The component does not implement a focus trap, allowing keyboard users to interact with page content behind the overlay while the modal is open. **WCAG:** 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap, 2.4.3 Focus Order **Perspective:** Keyboard & Motor Access **Severity:** MAJOR **Route to:** Front-End Dev (secondary: UX Design) **Evidence:** `SubscribeModal` component lacks focus management logic; CSS `.modal-backdrop` uses `position: fixed` but does not disable or hide background nav links. Focus order follows DOM insertion, which places modal content after the trigger in source order but visually centers it via flexbox. **Fix:** Implement a focus trap using a library like `focus-trap-react` or custom logic to keep Tab/Shift+Tab within `.modal-container`. Add `tabindex="-1"` to background nav links while modal is open, or use `aria-hidden="true"` on the background content. ``` #### Screen Reader & Semantic Structure ``` **Finding:** The modal container is a generic `
` missing `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal="true"`. Screen readers will not announce it as a dialog or understand its purpose, breaking the expected interaction model for blind users. **WCAG:** 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; WAI-ARIA APG Dialog Pattern **Perspective:** Screen Reader & Semantic Structure **Severity:** CRITICAL **Route to:** Front-End Dev (secondary: UX Design) **Evidence:** `
` in JSX (line ~108) lacks ARIA attributes. No `aria-labelledby` links it to the heading. **Fix:** Add `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` to the modal container. Associate it with the heading using `aria-labelledby="modal-title"`. Ensure the trigger button has `aria-expanded={isOpen}`. ``` ``` **Finding:** The close button uses a Unicode multiplication sign "×" without an accessible name. Screen readers will announce "button ×", which is meaningless to users relying on auditory feedback. **WCAG:** 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; 2.5.3 Label in Name **Perspective:** Screen Reader & Semantic Structure **Severity:** MAJOR **Route to:** Content Author (secondary: Front-End Dev) **Evidence:** `` (line ~29 and ~68) lacks `aria-label` or visible text. **Fix:** Add `aria-label="Close"` to the button, or replace "×" with a `×` and add visible text "Close". ``` ``` **Finding:** The success message ("Thanks, {name}! You're subscribed.") is rendered as a static paragraph when `submitted` becomes true. It is not announced to screen readers because it lacks an `aria-live` region. **WCAG:** 4.1.3 Status Messages **Perspective:** Screen Reader & Semantic Structure **Severity:** MINOR **Route to:** Front-End Dev (secondary: UX Design) **Evidence:** `

` in JSX is static DOM insertion without live region attributes. **Fix:** Wrap the success message in a `

` or route it through a notification/toast component that handles live announcements. ``` #### Cognitive & Neurodivergent ``` **Finding:** The name and email inputs lack `autocomplete` attributes. This forces users with cognitive load challenges or motor impairments to retype information, degrading the experience and increasing error risk. **WCAG:** 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose **Perspective:** Cognitive & Neurodivergent **Severity:** MINOR **Route to:** Front-End Dev (secondary: Content Author) **Evidence:** `` and `` in JSX lack `autocomplete` props. **Fix:** Add `autocomplete="name"` to the name input and `autocomplete="email"` to the email input. ``` ``` **Finding:** Closing the modal discards any typed form data without warning or confirmation. While not strictly a WCAG AA failure, it creates unnecessary cognitive load for users who close accidentally or navigate away mid-form. **WCAG:** 3.3.4 Error Prevention (Minimally) **Perspective:** Cognitive & Neurodivergent **Severity:** ENHANCEMENT **Route to:** UX Design (secondary: Front-End Dev) **Evidence:** `handleClose` sets `isOpen(false)` immediately without checking `email` or `name` state. **Fix:** Add a confirmation dialog or warning when closing if form fields contain data, or implement draft persistence/localStorage recovery. ``` ### Findings by Severity | Severity | Count | |---|---| | CRITICAL | 1 | | MAJOR | 2 | | MINOR | 2 | | ENHANCEMENT | 1 | ### Perspectives That Passed - Magnification & Reflow (not escalated) - Environmental Contrast (not escalated) - Vestibular & Motion Sensitivity (not escalated) - Auditory Access (not escalated) - *Note: Keyboard & Motor, Screen Reader, and Cognitive perspectives contained findings as detailed above.* ### Perspectives With Findings — Grouped by ARRM Role **Front-End Dev** - Missing focus trap on modal dialog — Keyboard & Motor — MAJOR — 2.1.2, 2.4.3 - Modal container missing `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal` — Screen Reader Semantic — CRITICAL — 4.1.2 - Success message lacks `aria-live` region — Screen Reader Semantic — MINOR — 4.1.3 - Form inputs missing `autocomplete` attributes — Cognitive & Neurodivergent — MINOR — 1.3.5 **Content Author** - Close button "×" lacks accessible name — Screen Reader Semantic — MAJOR — 4.1.2, 2.5.3 **UX Design** - No confirmation/warning on unsaved changes when closing modal — Cognitive & Neurodivergent — ENHANCEMENT — 3.3.4 ### Open Questions Requiring Human Verification - None. All findings were verified through source code review and CSS inspection. No content-level boundaries (captions, transcripts, alt text quality, reading level) were present in this component to require human verification. ### Recommended Next Step **REVISE** — MAJOR and CRITICAL findings are present. Address the missing focus trap, add `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal`, and provide an accessible name for the close button before shipping. The MINOR and ENHANCEMENT items should be scheduled for the next sprint to improve cognitive load and screen reader parity.
